submission.natural_language_explanation: L1/H6 is a broad copy head, not a detector: at every token it spreads attention over itself, the previous few words and a long tail of earlier context (mean weight 0.11 on itself, 0.12 on the previous token, the rest beyond that; it locks 0.8+ onto one token at only ~3% of positions) and writes that attention-weighted average of token values, so its strength |W_O(z-zbar)| is the distance of that average from its mean write and is large (1.0-3.0, 0.33-1.0 of max) exactly where the copy is dominated by a token far from the mean: demonstrative 'that'/'That is' (peak on the following word, 'that bill/town/letter/film' 1.0-2.5), 'this'/'these'/'Those' (0.7-1.7), expletive or subject 'it' (peak on the copula and adjective of 'it is / It has been X', 1.8-2.0), other pronouns ('I', 'you', 'we', 'they', 0.7-1.3) and rare content tokens such as proper nouns, money, unit and sports terms, split subwords and non-Latin-script words ('$2.4 billion', '247 yards', 'champion', 'Football', 1.0-3.0). Because nearly every text contains one such token, ordinary text of 8+ tokens is predicted active-weak somewhere (plain prose 22/25 measured at 0.78-2.31, median 1.06, usually on the noun after the determiner or the verb after the subject; even 4-6 token common-word sentences 7/8 at 0.67-1.9), and the only class that reliably stays below 0.25 x max is a bare comma-separated list of plain cardinal numbers - digits or number words, optional minus signs and decimal points, no other letters, no $ % = ; / or other symbols - which peaks at 0.0-0.41 (30/30 measured).
